status: research-only guidance. Nothing here is validated; only the F1 live button test (BUTN/UDP Action) can verify a control in-app, and only the owner's live test validates it.

evidence_labels.V: stated in an official manual, quick guide, product page or platform doc (read directly)
evidence_labels.A: inferred from official figures/tables or several official statements; not stated in words
evidence_labels.U: community, retailer or press source, or not checked; treat as unverified
evidence_labels.D: pitwall design proposal (derivation), not a hardware fact

layers: physical control on the rim/hub/module (what the driver touches)
signal the base/hub reports to the host, per platform (PS / Xbox / PC)
game binding (what the game does with that signal; may be none)
pitwall visibility (telemetry button bit, telemetry effect, PC HID, or nothing)

control_kinds.shift_paddle: momentary paddle; a button with a gear role
control_kinds.toggle_latching: maintained 2-position switch; reports a held state (or a pulse per change, device-specific)
control_kinds.toggle_momentary: spring-return rocker/toggle (up/down); reports as two buttons
control_kinds.encoder: endless detented rotary or thumb wheel; reports CW and CCW as two short button pulses; optional push button
control_kinds.multi_position: absolute N-position rotary (8/12-way); presentation depends on a mode (see mps_modes)
control_kinds.funky_7way: 4 directions + push + rotate (Fanatec FunkySwitch, Moza/Simagic 7-way); directions usually D-pad/hat, push a button, rotation an encoder pair
control_kinds.dpad_hat: 4/8-way pad, hat or 5-way stick (D-stick) with optional centre push
control_kinds.analogue_paddle: analogue axis 0..1 (clutch, dual clutch, handbrake, throttle, brake or free axis); role set by a mode
control_kinds.mode_selector: hardware switch that changes the rim's own behaviour; no output to the game
control_kinds.device_menu: control consumed by the hardware (tuning/settings/display menus); no output to the game
control_kinds.virtual_layer: selector that makes the same physical controls emit different signals (layers); state usually invisible to the host

signal_kinds.pad: a standard console pad input. PS: cross, circle, square, triangle, l1, r1, l2, r2, l3, r3, options, create, ps, dpad_up/down/left/right. Xbox: a, b, x, y, lb, rb, lt, rt, lsb, rsb, view, menu, xbox, dpad_*, next_gear, previous_gear
signal_kinds.game_specific: extra console input that only games with explicit support read (Fanatec 'GSB n' on PS and Xbox; Logitech items marked '*'; Thrustmaster encoders E1-E4 and mini-sticks on PS)
signal_kinds.folded: console input shared with other controls (e.g. Thrustmaster encoders become D-pad on Xbox; two different rim buttons both send A); the game cannot tell them apart
signal_kinds.hid_button: PC button number as printed by the maker (1-based)
signal_kinds.hid_axis: PC axis (X, Y, Z, Rx, Ry, Rz, Slider0, Slider1)

mps_modes.enc: two buttons, one per rotation direction (Fanatec ENC) [V]
mps_modes.pulse: one button per position, sent as a single pulse on change (Fanatec PULSE) [V]
mps_modes.constant: one button per position, held while in that position (Fanatec CONST) [V]
mps_modes.auto: the game chooses (Fanatec AUTO; needs game support) [V]
mps_modes.moza_knob: MOZA knobs: 'button or dial' modes (support spec sheet, via search) [A]
mps_modes.binary_coded: N positions encoded as combinations of a few buttons; DIY/community pattern, no brand source found [U]
mps_modes.axis_bands: positions read as bands of one analogue axis (resistor ladder); DIY/community pattern, no brand source found [U]

platform_rules.rule: PlayStation is unlocked by a PS-licensed base; Xbox by an Xbox-licensed steering wheel or hub; combine both for both consoles; any Fanatec rim on a PS-licensed base works on PS
rim features can depend on the base: the GT DD Pro wheel's four extra 5-way sticks are not available on ClubSport V2 / CSL Elite (V1.1) bases

separate PS/PC and Xbox/PC versions (G923, PRO, RS50, RS Wheel Hub PC vs Xbox); some wheel buttons need game support on console; PRO/RS50 can re-enumerate as an older wheel (G923 / PRO compatibility mode)

the base sets the platform (T248 PS vs T248X Xbox; T-GT II PS; TS-PC Racer PC); add-on rims fit several bases; on Xbox 'some features (encoders, number of action buttons) are limited by the console protocol'
PC by default; Xbox only with the Xbox-licensed R3 bundle or the ESX wheel; PlayStation not supported by current bases; PS5 bases (R5S Pro, R16S Ultra) announced Sept 2026, pending Sony approval
Xbox partnership announced; Xbox needs an Xbox-compatible base and an Xbox-compatible wheel; which models qualify not checked; no PS
PC only as far as found (Simucube docs only mention PC software; Simagic/Cammus PC-only per retailers)

console_limits.fact: Windows.Gaming.Input RacingWheelButtons: PreviousGear, NextGear, D-pad x4, Button1-16 (button assignment varies per controller and is meant for a user mapping UI)
GDK GameInputRacingWheelButtons: Menu, View, PreviousGear, NextGear, D-pad x4; A/B/X/Y, shoulders and thumbstick clicks are copied from the gamepad report

extra rim controls are folded onto the standard set or dropped: T248X encoders -> D-pad; SF1000 duplicates A/Y/LB/RB and loses DAP position 4; Fanatec MPS no output, encoders -> LT/RT; MOZA ESX disables some buttons; LSB/RSB only in some games (Thrustmaster, MOZA)
beyond the DualSense-style set, wheels expose extra inputs that only supporting games read (Fanatec GSB, Logitech '*', Thrustmaster encoders/mini-sticks). Sony's wheel input spec is not public
DirectInput DIJOYSTATE2: 128 buttons, 4 POV hats, 6 axes + 2 sliders. WinMM JOYINFOEX: 32 buttons, 6 axes, 1 POV. Older games can miss buttons above 32 (e.g. Fanatec MPS 37-76, PBMR 99/100)
Simucube Link Hub appears as one game controller with 128 buttons and 8 axes; each wheel's buttons are auto-mapped to slots; unmapped buttons produce no input

pitwall_visibility.telemetry_button: F1 25 Event BUTN buttonStatus: pad-equivalent bits (Cross/A ... Right Stick dirs, Special) plus UDP Action 1-12 (0x00100000 << n-1). UDP Actions are bound in the game's controls to any input the game can see. Only verifiable path.
pitwall_visibility.telemetry_effect: a setting/state changed in telemetry, so some control was used, but not which one: F1 brake bias, ERS mode, fuel mix, pit limiter, DRS/active aero; GT7 handbrake and headlight flags; Forza handbrake axis; PC sims (ACC TC/ABS/map/BB via shared memory, iRacing driver-control variables) need a Windows relay
pitwall_visibility.platform_hint: F1 Participants m_platform (1 Steam, 3 PlayStation, 4 Xbox, 6 Origin) picks the PS/Xbox/PC column; GT7 is always PlayStation
pitwall_visibility.pc_hid: only when the game and pitwall run on the same Windows PC; not implemented
pitwall_visibility.pitwall_own: on-screen PTT exists; a Bluetooth keyboard-type remote paired to the iPad could send key events to the dashboard page [D, untested]
pitwall_visibility.never: on console pitwall never sees the wheel itself, its rim id, unbound game-specific buttons, encoder layers or hardware mode selectors
